rationale: Password manager users are established paying buyers (1Password, Bitwarden), so commercial intent exists, but the buyer is primarily an individual consumer/power user rather than a business buyer with a budget line — this limits ARPU and makes a sustainable B2B pitch difficult. More critically, a browser extension that overrides site-level autocomplete attributes requires native browser extension development (JavaScript, manifest V3, platform-specific review and signing), which is entirely outside the Claude + prompts + Stripe factory tooling — buildability_with_ai scores a 2. Even if outsourced to a developer, the operational model would be viable (one-time purchase, automated delivery), but the factory cannot build this itself.
solution_plan: WHAT: A browser extension (Chrome/Firefox) that re-enables autofill on sites that have blocked it via autocomplete=off attributes. BUILD: This requires a JavaScript browser extension — it cannot be built by the Claude factory with its current tooling (prompts, forms, Stripe). A solo non-technical operator could not realistically build this without hiring a developer; if that route is taken, the factory could handle the landing page, Stripe payment link, and email delivery of the extension file. SELL: Target 1Password and Bitwarden community forums, r/privacy, and r/sysadmin — the factory can draft outreach copy for operator approval. MAINTAIN: Once built, delivery is a file download after Stripe payment; support is light (Claude handles FAQ); billing is automated via Stripe — operationally clean if the build problem is solved. VERDICT: Do not build with this factory alone. Validate demand cheaply (post a waitlist, gauge sign-ups) before spending on a developer.
notes: buildability_with_ai gate fails (scored 2 vs floor of 6) — this cannot be built with Claude + standard factory tooling. Stage capped at validate.
